title: Admin proxylet for smart remediation and stepwise runbook tasks
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a lightweight admin proxy component ("proxylet") that transforms existing runbook steps into idempotent, observable tasks that can be executed by support engineers and by the automated remediator. Goals: 1) enable step-level retry and checkpointing so long-running fixes can resume; 2) attach structured telemetry and human-visible audit trails to each step; 3) provide an execution adapter that maps existing scripts/CLI actions to sandboxed operations with safety gating.
background: We currently have many long-form runbooks and ad-hoc admin scripts. Automated remediation attempts are brittle because steps are not idempotent, lack structured outputs, and provide poor signal for rollbacks. Oncall feedback from the Feb incident (INC-2026-02-07) highlighted three repeatable failures where manual intervention was necessary because the tooling could not resume mid-playbook. This ticket proposes a proxylet shim to: standardize step contracts, record step-level evidence for audits, and allow automated and manual execution to share the same primitives.
steps: Design step contract schema (inputs, outputs, idempotency hints, timeout, safety checks).
Implement proxylet runtime that wraps script/command execution in a containerized sandbox with retries and checkpointing.
Create adapters for common admin actions: k8s rollout pause/resume, infra scaling, cache invalidation, user token revocation.
Integrate structured telemetry: per-step traces, success/failure reasons, artifacts attached to step execution in the Console.
Add safety policy layer that enforces allowlists, dry-run mode, and escalation hooks for high-risk steps.
Wire proxylet into the runbooks-as-tasks engine so runbooks can be executed stepwise and resumed from checkpoints.
End-to-end QA and canary: run synthetic incident scenarios in Ops Lab and validate rollback / resume behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Proxylet can execute a step and persist its result and metadata to the runbook store with <30s overhead.
A paused or failed multi-step runbook can be resumed from the last successful step without manual rework.
All executed steps emit structured telemetry visible in Console traces and link back to the originating runbook ticket.
Safety policies block execution of high-risk steps unless explicit approval is provided; dry-run returns planned changes only.
Adapters exist for at least three common admin domains (k8s, infra-scaling, and cache-layer).

open_questions: Should proxylet expose a human-facing CLI vs only HTTP API for oncall ergonomics?
How do we model nested steps (compound actions) for rollback semantics?
When migrating legacy scripts, do we rewrite them as typed adapters or embed a compatibility wrapper first?
